children.value: , the geometry of the trajectory is a hyperbola. The shape of a hyperbola is two symmetric, disconnected curves. The body following the trajectory occupies one of the curves. The other is an empty, imaginary orbit present only due to the mathematics.

All interplanetary bodies such as comets or asteroids that approach the Earth, or any spacecraft we want to send to other planets, must be on a hyperbolic trajectory. Whereas a parabolic trajectory has zero velocity at infinite radius, the hyperbolic trajectory has some nonzero velocity.

Periapsis lies on the apse line, as usual, of the occupied trajectory. Interestingly, apoapsis lies on the virtual trajectory. Halfway between periapsis and apoapsis lies the center of a Cartesian coordinate system.
